etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Latin īnspector, from īnspiciō.

definitions.definition: A person employed to inspect something.

quote.citation: 2013 July 19, Peter Wilby, “Finland spreads word on schools”, in The Guardian Weekly, volume 189, number 6, page 30:
quote.text: Imagine a country where children do nothing but play until they start compulsory schooling at age seven. Then, without exception, they attend comprehensives until the age of 16. […] There are no inspectors, no exams until the age of 18, no school league tables, no private tuition industry, no school uniforms. […]

definitions.definition: (law enforcement) A police officer ranking below superintendent.
(computing) A software tool used to examine something.

quote.text: Chrome has a built-in development tool called the Chrome Inspector. You can use it to examine the HTML elements in a web page; review what resources — or files, cookies, and databases — are active; follow network activity;  […]

quote.citation: 2020, Anatoly Belous, Vitali Saladukha, Viruses, Hardware and Software Trojans, page 112:
quote.text: After that, with the help of the disk inspector, you can at any time compare the status of programs and system disk areas with the original one.
